| where EventID == 4688

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Exploitation. [LLM] Grandoreiro DLL side-load: libwebp/mingw10/libffi-6/libpng15 loaded from user-writable paths Installation High
Hunts for the four Grandoreiro-associated DLLs (libwebp.dll, mingw10.dll, libffi-6.dll, libpng15.dll) being loaded outside their canonical Program Files / Windows locations. WatchGuard observed these specific filenames side-loaded by FastStone Image Viewer, MinGW, FreeMat, and AbiWord — the classic 'legit binary + adjacent attacker DLL' tell. Rationale: Targets the four DLL filenames explicitly named in the WatchGuard report and the trusted host binaries documented (FastStone, MinGW, FreeMat, AbiWord). Side-load tell = the named DLL appearing outside Program Files/Windows. Cross-checked with THN's parallel WatchGuard write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grandoreiro-malware-and-btmob-rat.html • https://securelist.com/grandoreiro-banking-trojan/114257/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("libwebp.dll","mingw10.dll","libffi-6.dll","libpng15.dll")
| where not (FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\" or FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\" or FolderPath startswith @"C:\Windows\")
| extend SideLoadHost = case(
    InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("FSViewer.exe","FastStoneViewer.exe"), "FastStone (libwebp expected)",
    InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("mingw32-make.exe","gcc.exe","g++.exe","ld.exe"), "MinGW (mingw10 expected)",
    InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "FreeMat.exe", "FreeMat (libffi-6 expected)",
    InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "AbiWord.exe", "AbiWord (libpng15 expected)",
    "Unexpected host")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SideLoadHost, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 7
| where EventData has_any ("libwebp.dll","mingw10.dll","libffi-6.dll","libpng15.dll")
| where not (EventData has @"\Program Files\" or EventData has @"\Program Files (x86)\" or EventData has @"\Windows\\System32\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventData

[LLM] Grandoreiro C2 beacon to 162.33.177.150 Command & Control High
Alerts on any outbound connection to the Grandoreiro C2 IP 162.33.177.150 disclosed in the WatchGuard report. Single high-fidelity IOC; ship as alerting until the IP rotates. Rationale: Single static IOC from the WatchGuard IoC table — Grandoreiro C2. High confidence because routable internet hits to this IP are not normal background traffic. Atomic IP indicator (not corroborated by a second public source beyond WatchGuard at time of writing — confidence drops to Medium if no other reports list it within 14 days). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grandoreiro-malware-and-btmob-rat.html

[LLM] Grandoreiro geolocation lookup: ip-api.com/json queried by wscript/cscript Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for wscript.exe or cscript.exe contacting ip-api.com — Grandoreiro's VBS dropper uses this public service to verify the victim is in a targeted region before unpacking the banker. Browser hits to ip-api.com are common; script-host hits are not. Rationale: Article explicitly cites hxxp://ip-api[.]com/json as the geolocation lookup, with the surrounding text confirming it's the VBS-dropped malware that performs the query. Pairing the well-known service with a non-browser parent (wscript/cscript) is the high-fidelity twist. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grandoreiro-malware-and-btmob-rat.html

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 22
| where EventData has "ip-api.com"
| where EventData has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")

[LLM] VBS-driven AntiVirusProduct enumeration via WMI SecurityCenter2 Actions on Objectives High
Detects script hosts (wscript.exe/cscript.exe) or their child wmic.exe querying root\\SecurityCenter2 / AntiVirusProduct / AntiSpywareProduct — exact pre-execution AV check performed by the Grandoreiro VBS dropper before it stages the banker. Rationale: The article explicitly shows the WMI-via-VBS AV check screenshot and states the script queries AV before proceeding. SecurityCenter2 namespace lookups from script hosts are extremely rare in real environments — this is high-fidelity intent. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grandoreiro-malware-and-btmob-rat.html
ATT&CKT1518.001 T1047 T1059.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("SecurityCenter2","AntiVirusProduct","AntiSpywareProduct","FirewallProduct")
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") and (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" or FileName =~ "powershell.exe" or FileName =~ "cmd.exe"))
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (CommandLine has "SecurityCenter2" or CommandLine has "AntiVirusProduct" or CommandLine has "AntiSpywareProduct" or CommandLine has "FirewallProduct")
| where ParentProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "wmic.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

[LLM] Grandoreiro phishing & C2 infrastructure DNS (byethost / contaboserver / uniaodownloadcnk) Command & Control High
Hunts DNS queries matching the Grandoreiro infra patterns: *.byethost<N>.com (C2), vmi<7-digit>.contaboserver.net (geofenced phishing pages), and the static phishing domain uniaodownloadcnk.online. Regex on the numeric subdomain shapes keeps the rule fresh as rotations happen. Rationale: Three article-named infra patterns: the static phishing domain (uniaodownloadcnk.online), the templated Contabo VPS naming (vmi<7-digit>.contaboserver.net), and the byethost C2 pattern. Regex on the digit-shape resists IP rotation. Contabo abuse pattern also corroborated in Securelist's Grandoreiro coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/grandoreiro-banking-trojan/114257/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grandoreiro-malware-and-btmob-rat.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001 T1566.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)\.byethost\d+\.com$")
   or (RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)^vmi\d{7}\.contaboserver\.net$")
   or RemoteUrl =~ "uniaodownloadcnk.online"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (Name matches regex @"(?i)\.byethost\d+\.com$")
   or (Name matches regex @"(?i)^vmi\d{7}\.contaboserver\.net$")
   or Name =~ "uniaodownloadcnk.online"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Grandoreiro delivery: ZIP/VBS dropped from Dropbox/Mediafire/Contabo to user-writable path Delivery Medium
Hunts files arriving from the article-named delivery surfaces (dropbox.com / dropboxusercontent.com / mediafire.com / uniaodownloadcnk.online / contaboserver.net) where the dropped name matches the campaign payloads — *.zip, *.vbs, or one of the four named DLLs. Rationale: Article explicitly names Dropbox + Mediafire + Contabo + uniaodownloadcnk.online as delivery surfaces and ZIP / VBS / the four DLLs as payload shapes. FileOriginUrl on Defender DeviceFileEvents ties the URL to the dropped file in one row — the cleanest available proxy for 'this file came from a Grandoreiro-aligned source'. Medium confidence because Dropbox/Mediafire are heavily used legitimately; tier alerting because the file-name combination is what discriminates. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/grandoreiro-malware-and-btmob-rat.html • https://securelist.com/grandoreiro-banking-trojan/114257/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1105 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Web.Web
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileOriginUrl has_any ("dropbox.com","dropboxusercontent.com","mediafire.com","uniaodownloadcnk.online","contaboserver.net")
| where FileName endswith ".zip"
    or FileName endswith ".vbs"
    or FileName in~ ("libwebp.dll","mingw10.dll","libffi-6.dll","libpng15.dll")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginIP, FileOriginReferrerUrl, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 15
| where EventData has_any ("dropbox.com","dropboxusercontent.com","mediafire.com","uniaodownloadcnk.online","contaboserver.net")
| where EventData has_any (".zip",".vbs","libwebp.dll","mingw10.dll","libffi-6.dll","libpng15.dll")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventData

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Tycoon 2FA AiTM - Node.js HTTP Client Sign-in to Microsoft Authentication Broker · [LLM] Tycoon 2FA Microsoft Authentication Broker Sign-in from Cheap-VPS ASN · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Tycoon 2FA AiTM - Node.js HTTP Client Sign-in to Microsoft Authentication Broker Command & Control High
Detects the Tier 1 Tycoon 2FA kit relay completing OAuth flows against the Microsoft Authentication Broker (AppId 29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e) using Node.js HTTP libraries (axios/node-fetch/undici). Legitimate Auth Broker traffic comes from Windows OS components and the Microsoft Authentication Library — Node.js user agents against this client ID are a near-pure kit signal. Rationale: Pairs the article's two strongest IOCs: the Microsoft Authentication Broker AppId 29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e (Tier 1 kit relay's OAuth client for device-code-grant + PRT minting) with the Node.js HTTP client user-agents (node, axios/1.15.2, node-fetch/1.0, undici). Legitimate Auth Broker sign-ins come from Windows OS / WAM with Windows-Microsoft-Auth user agents — Node.js UAs against this specific client are pathognomonic for Tycoon 2FA. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/tycoon-2fa-aitm-detection-engineering • https://www.esentire.com/blog/tycoon-2fa-operators-adopt-oauth-device-code-phishing • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/tycoon2fa-hijacks-microsoft-365-accounts-via-device-code-phishing/
ATT&CKT1557 T1528 T1078.004

AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ApplicationId =~ "29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e"  // Microsoft Authentication Broker — abused by Tycoon 2FA for PRT minting
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where UserAgent matches regex @"(?i)^(node($|\b|/|,)|axios/[0-9]|node-fetch/[0-9]|undici)"
| extend ParsedNet = parse_json(NetworkLocationDetails)
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, AccountObjectId, ApplicationId, Application, UserAgent, IPAddress, Country, City, IsAnonymousProxy, ConditionalAccessStatus, AuthenticationRequirement, DeviceTrustType, IsCompliantUser, RequestId
| order by Timestamp desc
SigninLogs

| where AppId =~ "29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e"  // Microsoft Authentication Broker — Tycoon 2FA kit relay target

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Tycoon 2FA Microsoft Authentication Broker Sign-in from Cheap-VPS ASN Command & Control Medium
Hunts successful sign-ins to the Microsoft Authentication Broker (29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e) sourced from the cheap-VPS ASNs the Tycoon 2FA Tier 1 relay infrastructure runs on (Alibaba Cloud, Clouvider). Catches kit relays whose UA was rotated away from the Node defaults, by pivoting on the second IOC dimension: source infrastructure. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'Alibaba Cloud (and similar cheap-VPS ASNs)' as Tier 1 kit relay infrastructure and 'Clouvider, Host Telecom' for the Google variant. Combined with the Auth Broker AppId, an enterprise should have ~zero legitimate Auth Broker sign-ins from these ASNs (consumer/Windows devices don't typically egress through Alibaba Cloud IPs). ASN list is verifiable in your tenant — adjust as new infra surfaces. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/tycoon-2fa-aitm-detection-engineering • https://www.esentire.com/blog/tycoon-2fa-operators-adopt-oauth-device-code-phishing
ATT&CKT1557 T1078.004 T1583.003

[LLM] Rogue Entra Device Registration Following Tycoon 2FA AiTM Sign-in (PRT Persistence) Installation High
Detects the Tycoon 2FA post-compromise persistence pattern: the kit registers a rogue device immediately after a successful AiTM sign-in to obtain a device-bound Primary Refresh Token that survives 'revoke sessions + reset password' remediation. Correlates a suspect Microsoft Authentication Broker sign-in with an 'Add device' AuditLog from the same principal within 1 hour. Rationale: Maps directly to the article's strongest persistence statement: 'The kit can register a rogue device in Entra ID, obtaining a primary refresh token that stays valid even after a defender revokes the compromised user's sessions.' Corroborated by Elastic and eSentire — the device-PRT chain is the reason the standard revoke-and-reset playbook fails. Correlating Auth Broker sign-in (UC1 conditions) with an 'Add device' event by the same principal within 1h is a near-pure Tycoon 2FA signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/tycoon-2fa-aitm-detection-engineering • https://www.esentire.com/blog/tycoon-2fa-operators-adopt-oauth-device-code-phishing • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/tycoon2fa-hijacks-microsoft-365-accounts-via-device-code-phishing/
ATT&CKT1098.005 T1556.007 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes Authentication
// Suspect Tycoon 2FA kit sign-ins → device registration via CloudAppEvents within 1h
let SuspectSignins = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ApplicationId =~ "29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e"
    | where ErrorCode == 0
    | where UserAgent matches regex @"(?i)^(node($|\b|/|,)|axios/[0-9]|node-fetch/[0-9]|undici)"
    | project SignInTime=Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountUpn, SrcIP=IPAddress, SignInRequestId=RequestId;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Azure Active Directory" or ApplicationId == 11161
| where ActionType in ("Add device", "Add registered owner to device", "Register device", "Add registered users to device")
| extend ActorUpn = tostring(AccountDisplayName)
| join kind=inner SuspectSignins on $left.AccountObjectId == $right.AccountObjectId
| where Timestamp between (SignInTime .. SignInTime + 1h)
| extend MinutesAfterSignIn = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, SignInTime)
| project SignInTime, DeviceRegTime=Timestamp, MinutesAfterSignIn, AccountObjectId, AccountUpn, SrcIP, IPAddress, ActionType, ObjectName, ObjectId, RawEventData
| order by DeviceRegTime desc
// Suspect Tycoon 2FA kit sign-ins → device registration in Entra AuditLogs within 1h
let SuspectSignins = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where AppId =~ "29d9ed98-a469-4536-ade2-f981bc1d605e"
    | where ResultType == 0
    | where UserAgent matches regex @"(?i)^(node($|\b|/|,)|axios/[0-9]|node-fetch/[0-9]|undici)"
       or AutonomousSystemNumber in (45102, 37963, 134963, 62240)
    | project SignInTime=TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName=tolower(UserPrincipalName), UserId, SrcIP=IPAddress, SignInASN=AutonomousSystemNumber, SignInUA=UserAgent, SignInRequestId=OriginalRequestId;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName in ("Add device", "Add registered owner to device", "Register device", "Add registered users to device")
| where Result == "success"
| extend ActorUpn = tolower(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName))
| extend ActorObjectId = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.id)
| extend ActorIP = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend DeviceName = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend DeviceId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| join kind=inner SuspectSignins on $left.ActorObjectId == $right.UserId
| where TimeGenerated between (SignInTime .. SignInTime + 1h)
| extend MinutesAfterSignIn = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, SignInTime)
| project SignInTime, DeviceRegTime=TimeGenerated, MinutesAfterSignIn, ActorUpn, ActorIP, SrcIP, SignInASN, SignInUA, OperationName, DeviceName, DeviceId
| order by DeviceRegTime desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:

    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] LiquidJS SSTI gadget tokens in inbound HTTP (CVE-2026-45618) Exploitation High
Hunts for LiquidJS template-injection PoC strings — `1|valueOf`, `r.context.scopes`, `r.liquid.parser`, `r.liquid.options.fs`, `assign __proto__`, `process.getBuiltinModule`, `child_process`, `execSync` — appearing in inbound URLs, query strings, referers, or form bodies served by IIS / App Service / WAF-fronted Node.js apps embedding LiquidJS templates. Rationale: Anchored to literal LiquidJS PoC tokens (`1|valueOf`, `r.context.scopes`, `r.liquid.parser`, `r.liquid.options.fs`, `assign __proto__`, `getBuiltinModule`, `child_process`, `execSync`, `fs.readFileSync`) — none of these are legitimate query-string contents and they are unique to the GHSA-gf2q-c269-pqgc gadget chain. Cross-checked against the GitHub advisory and the LiquidJS NPM page for fix version 10.26.0. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gf2q-c269-pqgc • https://www.npmjs.com/package/liquidjs • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007

   or AdditionalFields has_any ("1|valueOf","r.context.scopes","r.liquid.parser","__proto__","getBuiltinModule","child_process")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, LocalPort, AdditionalFields

[LLM] Node.js web process spawning shell (LiquidJS RCE post-exploit) Exploitation High
Detects `node.exe` (or Linux `node`) — and IIS-hosted Node via `iisnode`/`w3wp.exe` running a Node app — spawning an interactive shell (`sh`, `bash`, `cmd.exe`, `powershell.exe`) immediately after the LiquidJS PoC executes `process.getBuiltinModule('child_process').execSync('sh', {stdio:'inherit'})`. This child-shell pattern is the deterministic post-exploit signal of CVE-2026-45618. Rationale: PoC ends with `process.getBuiltinModule('child_process').execSync('sh', {stdio:'inherit'})` — so the deterministic post-exploitation signal is `node` (or `w3wp.exe` hosting `iisnode`) becoming the parent of an interactive shell. node→sh is exceedingly rare in production: Node apps almost never `exec` a TTY-bearing shell. Cross-checked against the GHSA PoC body and standard Node.js production process trees. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gf2q-c269-pqgc • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1059 T1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","w3wp.exe","iisnode.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessTokenElevation, ProcessIntegrityLevel, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","\\node","/node","w3wp.exe","iisnode.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","\\sh","/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh","\\bash.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, EventVendor, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] msiexec.exe installs MSI from DinDoor fake-installer infrastructure (GitHub/SourceForge) Delivery High
Detects the DinDoor delivery vector where a user pastes the attacker-supplied terminal command, which invokes msiexec.exe to download and silently install an MSI hosted on the campaign's GitHub/SourceForge repos or claudescript.top. Parent is a console (cmd/powershell/Windows Terminal), not the usual InstallShield/Edge download. Rationale: Anchors on the exact campaign infrastructure named in the article (claudescript.top, the three GitHub repos, the two SourceForge project slugs) plus the terminal-paste delivery vector described in the body. msiexec spawned by an interactive shell with a URL argument is unusual outside attacker-instructed copy-paste installs.
ATT&CKT1218.007 T1204.002 T1608.001

| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("claudescript.top","claude-free-plugin","ai-gen-profi","wharfdemolisherpit","sourceforge.net/projects/gearup","sourceforge.net/projects/bluewaveremover")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/i","/quiet","/qn","http://","https://")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256

[LLM] PowerShell installs Deno runtime via Scoop/WinGet then executes remote script (DinDoor stager) Installation High
Detects the DinDoor stager step where the dropped PowerShell script uses Scoop or WinGet to install the Deno JavaScript runtime, then immediately invokes deno to fetch and run the backdoor from the attacker's server. The legitimate-package-manager-as-LOLBin pattern is the article's stated defense-evasion trick. Rationale: Article specifically calls out Scoop and WinGet being abused to install Deno as a stealthy stager, with deno.exe then running the DinDoor payload from a remote URL. The Deno-with-broad-permissions + remote URL combination is the article's distinctive execution fingerprint.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.007 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("scoop","deno") and ProcessCommandLine has "install")
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "winget" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DenoLand.Deno","denoland.deno","install deno"))
    or (FileName =~ "deno.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--allow-all","--allow-net"," -A "," run ") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","claudescript.top","workers.dev","duckdns.org"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where (CommandLine has_all ("scoop","deno") and CommandLine has "install")
    or (CommandLine has "winget" and CommandLine has_any ("DenoLand.Deno","denoland.deno","install deno"))
    or (NewProcessName endswith @"\deno.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("--allow-all","--allow-net"," -A "," run ") and CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","claudescript.top","workers.dev","duckdns.org"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DinDoor Deno Runtime Stager via Scoop or WinGet

[LLM] Outbound connection to DinDoor C2 infrastructure (specific domains and IPs) Command & Control High
Network detection for any host beaconing to the C2 set published by Malwarebytes: ms-telemetry-gateway-us.com, dakatawebstick.com, ashpaltlonpro.com, agilemast3r.duckdns.org, geralnewlong.com, hngfbgfbfb.cyou, logicalnewrestore.com, claudescript.top, the Cloudflare Workers proxy, and five hardcoded IPs. Rationale: Direct IOC match on the full domain + IP set published in the article. Cloudflare Workers C2 (cf-proxy.cloud-analytics-services.workers.dev) deserves special attention because the article notes the lite agent uses it for anonymity; matching the full subdomain (not just workers.dev) keeps FP rate low.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.001 T1102.002 T1568.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web

union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceNetworkEvents

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] DinDoor persistence: Run-key value pointing to Deno or DinDoor C2 infrastructure Installation High
Detects the article's stated persistence mechanism — a Windows Registry Run key written by the DinDoor backdoor that re-launches the Deno-based payload on boot. Anchors on Deno binary path, DinDoor C2 hostnames in the value data, and the specific Deno permission flags the RAT requires. Rationale: Article explicitly states 'DinDoor then establishes persistence by creating a Windows registry run key.' Anchoring on deno.exe + permissive flags catches the runtime path; anchoring on the C2 hostnames in value data catches variants where the Run key invokes a one-liner that contacts the C2 directly.
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in~ ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("deno.exe","deno run","--allow-all","--allow-net","claudescript.top","ms-telemetry-gateway-us.com","dakatawebstick.com","ashpaltlonpro.com","agilemast3r.duckdns.org","geralnewlong.com","hngfbgfbfb.cyou","logicalnewrestore.com","cf-proxy.cloud-analytics-services.workers.dev")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated","set","create")
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("deno.exe","deno run","--allow-all","--allow-net","claudescript.top","ms-telemetry-gateway-us.com","dakatawebstick.com","ashpaltlonpro.com","agilemast3r.duckdns.org","geralnewlong.com","hngfbgfbfb.cyou","logicalnewrestore.com","cf-proxy.cloud-analytics-services.workers.dev")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Hidden Microsoft Edge process spawned by deno.exe for covert screen streaming (DinDoor RAT) Actions on Objectives High
Detects DinDoor's signature stealth-streaming capability: deno.exe launches a hidden msedge.exe process and uses it as a covert browser-rendered video stream to the attacker. Filters on the rare deno→msedge parent/child relationship combined with headless/hidden/remote-debugging Edge flags. Rationale: Article explicitly describes a unique TTP: 'silently launches a hidden Edge process, injects a small web page into it, and uses that page to stream live video of the victim's screen directly to the attacker.' The parent-child pair deno.exe→msedge.exe with headless/remote-debugging flags is essentially zero-FP in any non-developer environment.
ATT&CKT1564.003 T1185 T1113
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "deno.exe"
| where FileName =~ "msedge.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--headless","--remote-debugging-port","--user-data-dir=","--app=","--window-position=-","--disable-gpu","--no-sandbox","--remote-debugging-pipe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\deno.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\msedge.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--headless","--remote-debugging-port","--user-data-dir=","--app=","--window-position=-","--disable-gpu","--no-sandbox","--remote-debugging-pipe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DinDoor Hidden Edge Spawned by Deno for Covert Screen Streaming
id: 9d3f7e21-5a6c-4b88-a14e-d72f6ac3e095
description: deno.exe spawns msedge.exe with headless/remote-debugging/hidden-window flags — the DinDoor RAT covert P2P video-streaming primitive.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-fake-chatgpt-and-claude-installers/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/27
tags:
  - attack.t1564.003
  - attack.t1185
  - attack.t1113
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\deno.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '\msedge.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--headless'
      - '--remote-debugging-port'
      - '--user-data-dir='
      - '--app='
      - '--window-position=-'
      - '--disable-gpu'
      - '--no-sandbox'
      - '--remote-debugging-pipe'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @ParentImage:(*\deno.exe OR *\DENO.EXE) @Image:(*\msedge.exe OR *\MSEDGE.EXE) @CommandLine:(*--headless* OR *--remote-debugging-port* OR *--user-data-dir=* OR *--app=* OR *--window-position=-* OR *--disable-gpu* OR *--no-sandbox* OR *--remote-debugging-pipe*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^deno\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\msedge\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(--headless|--remote-debugging-port|--user-data-dir=|--app=|--window-position=-|--disable-gpu|--no-sandbox|--remote-debugging-pipe)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=deno.exe AND Processes.process_name=msedge.exe AND (Processes.process="*--headless*" OR Processes.process="*--remote-debugging-port*" OR Processes.process="*--user-data-dir=*" OR Processes.process="*--app=*" OR Processes.process="*--window-position=-*" OR Processes.process="*--disable-gpu*" OR Processes.process="*--no-sandbox*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=deno.exe AND Processes.process_name=msedge.exe AND (Processes.process="*--headless*" OR Processes.process="*--remote-debugging-port*" OR Processes.process="*--user-data-dir=*" OR Processes.process="*--app=*" OR Processes.process="*--window-position=-*" OR Processes.process="*--disable-gpu*" OR Processes.process="*--no-sandbox*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.227.196.107", "45.137.99.121", "31.57.129.23", "66.78.40.107", "193.233.198.132") or RemoteUrl has_any ("claudescript.top", "ms-telemetry-gateway-us.com", "dakatawebstick.com", "ashpaltlonpro.com", "cf-proxy.cloud-analytics-services.workers.dev", "agilemast3r.duckdns.org", "geralnewlong.com", "hngfbgfbfb.cyou", "logicalnewrestore.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,

let BadDomains = dynamic(["claudescript.top", "ms-telemetry-gateway-us.com", "dakatawebstick.com", "ashpaltlonpro.com", "cf-proxy.cloud-analytics-services.workers.dev", "agilemast3r.duckdns.org", "geralnewlong.com", "hngfbgfbfb.cyou", "logicalnewrestore.com"]);

Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |

    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:

    condition: selection_image and selection_args

      cross-shell escaping

[LLM] forge-jsxy npm RAT C2 to 204.10.194.247 (WebSocket 9877 / HTTP 8765) Command & Control High
Detects outbound connections from node/npm-driven processes to the forge-jsxy/forge-jsx C2 server at 204.10.194.247 on the WebSocket relay (TCP 9877) or HTTP exfil API (TCP 8765). Hard-coded infrastructure shared across both package generations makes this the highest-fidelity pivot in the campaign. Rationale: 204.10.194.247:9877 (WebSocket relay) and :8765 (HTTP exfil) are hard-coded campaign C2 endpoints confirmed by SafeDep and the article's IOC table. Both ports are non-standard and bound to a single residential-range IP, making any hit high-confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-forge-jsxy-npm-rat-evolution/ • https://safedep.io/malicious-forge-jsx-npm-rat/

[LLM] forge-jsxy durable agent directory created outside node_modules Installation High
Hunts for file writes into the CfgMgr/.forge-jsxy durable persistence directory that the malware drops on disk so that npm uninstall leaves the agent running. Uses the platform-specific paths from the SafeDep IOC table — these directory names are unique to the campaign. Rationale: The article's IOC table lists the exact persistence directory on all three platforms: %LOCALAPPDATA%\CfgMgr\data.forge-jsxy\ (Windows), ~/.local/share/cfgmgr/.forge-jsxy/ (Linux), and ~/Library/Application Support/CfgMgr/data/.forge-jsxy/ (macOS). SafeDep's write-up confirms the directory persists across npm uninstall — any file event here is the malware itself. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-forge-jsxy-npm-rat-evolution/ • https://safedep.io/malicious-forge-jsx-npm-rat/

[LLM] forge-jsxy Windows persistence: ForgeJSWorker Run key / Scheduled Task Installation High
Detects creation of the ForgeJSWorker Run-key value or the ForgeJSWorker scheduled task — the two named Windows persistence mechanisms documented in the SafeDep IOC table. These names are campaign-specific and not used by any benign product. Rationale: The article specifies the exact Windows persistence artefacts: 'Task Scheduler: ForgeJSWorker' and 'HKCU…\Run\ForgeJSWorker'. The ForgeJSWorker name is unique to this campaign — Run-key value names are flat strings, so an exact-name match has effectively zero benign FPs. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-forge-jsxy-npm-rat-evolution/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
union
(DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" and RegistryValueName =~ "ForgeJSWorker")
        or RegistryValueData has "forge-jsxy"
        or RegistryValueData has @"CfgMgr\data\.forge-jsxy"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("ScheduledTaskCreated","ScheduledTaskUpdated")
| where AdditionalFields has "ForgeJSWorker" or ProcessCommandLine has "ForgeJSWorker" or FolderPath has "ForgeJSWorker"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" and RegistryValue =~ "ForgeJSWorker")
        or RegistryValueData has "forge-jsxy"
        or RegistryValueData has @"CfgMgr\data\.forge-jsxy"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData),
(SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4698 // scheduled task created
| where EventData has "ForgeJSWorker" or EventData has "forge-jsxy"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, EventID, EventData)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] forge-jsxy crypto-wallet secret vault write (.vault/secret-audit/result.json) Actions on Objectives High
Detects file writes to the malware's hidden secret-audit vault that stores harvested wallet keys, seed phrases and credentials after BIP39/cryptographic validation. The vault path is unique to the forge-jsxy campaign and indicates active credential exfiltration staging on the host. Rationale: The IOC table names the exact vault path '<durable>/.vault/secret-audit/result.json' as the destination for cryptographically-validated wallet keys. SafeDep's write-up confirms this is the staging vault that persists across reboots and package removal. The path string is unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-forge-jsxy-npm-rat-evolution/ • https://safedep.io/malicious-forge-jsx-npm-rat/
ATT&CKT1555 T1005 T1074.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.vault\secret-audit" or FolderPath has "/.vault/secret-audit")
| where FileName =~ "result.json"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.vault\secret-audit" or TargetFilePath has "/.vault/secret-audit")
| where TargetFileName =~ "result.json"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
